content.title: 49 Patients Under Treatment at Aga Khan University Hospital for Viral Haemorrhagic Fever
content.summary: At Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH), 49 patients are currently hospitalized with suspect viral haemorrhagic fever; most of them were admitted during the last two weeks.

media.alt: 49 Patients Under Treatment at Aga Khan University Hospital for Viral Haemorrhagic Fever

content.text: At Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH), 49 patients are currently hospitalized with suspect viral haemorrhagic fever; most of them were admitted during the last two weeks. This obviously reflects a sudden increase in the number of such cases and is a cause of concern. So far, a total of 175 patients with ages ranging between 6 to 82 years were admitted at AKUH between June 14 to October 17, 2006 with viral haemorrhagic fever. Out of these, six patients expired due to severity of disease, while 120 recovered and were discharged. The patients suffered from symptoms ranging from bleeding, diarrhoea, vomiting to abdominal pain.

Sixty-five patients were diagnosed to have Dengue hemorrhagic fever, three patients suffered from Crimean-Congo Haemorrhagic Fever (CCHF), while in the remaining, the special serological tests were either negative or the results are pending. A total of 168 patients were received from Karachi and the remaining patients came from Larkana, Hyderabad, Gilgit, Baluchistan and Saudi Arabia.
Dr Farhat Abbas Medical Director and Associate Dean, Clinical Affairs, Aga Khan University Hospital.
